SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Parts of the Body Suggested vocabulary Head, hand, leg, eye, ear, nose, neck, fi in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we say words and sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 8.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: Learning independently is enhanced as the learner work on their own to practise matching vocabulary to pictures or picture

descriptions.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and effectively is developed as they use new words learnt in relevant

contexts.

Values:
Responsibility: A learner takes different roles while engaging in pair activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem) –Learners acquire an enhanced level of self-esteem as they write legibly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

All Learning Areas require proper spelling and good handwriting/braille writing.

Suggested learning resources

• Audio, video clip,

• Wall charts/braille charts/pattern books,

• Objects,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.
